lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
On the same grid the shop is at B3 and the school is at E3. In which direction is the school from the shop, and how many squares?

FEEDBACK
East, three squares. Both are in row 3, and E is three columns right of B.

WATCH FOR
Reading rows before columns, or counting the starting square, gives the wrong square or wrong distance.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Use an atlas or online map of Australia to locate eight places. Write relative location sentences for each, and give grid references from a class grid. Name the atlas you used.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Use an atlas or online map of Australia to locate eight places. Write relative location sentences for each, and give grid references from a class grid. Name the atlas you used. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Example: Darwin is north of Alice Springs, and Adelaide is south of it. On a classroom grid with columns A to F left to right and rows 1 to 6 from the top, the library is at D3 and the park is at D6. The park is three squares south of the library.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Reading rows before columns, or counting the starting square, gives the wrong square or wrong distance. Correction: East, three squares. Both are in row 3, and E is three columns right of B.

Parent: Likely misconception: Reading rows before columns, or counting the starting square, gives the wrong square or wrong distance. Keep sample answers out of the child role.
